subject: Cognitive Science
title: Choice Overload
description: A short lesson to help you apply Choice Overload.

hook.text: A store offers 24 jams for tasting. Another offers 6. The 6-jam table sells ten times more. Less was more.

buildup.text: Choice overload: too many options paralyze decision-making and reduce satisfaction with the final pick.

discovery.text: Sheena Iyengar's jam study showed that abundance creates anxiety. Every option you skip feels like a loss.

twist.text: It doesn't always apply. Experts handle more choices than novices, and desire for variety reduces the effect.

climax.text: Good design reduces choices: curated defaults, categories, and recommendations fight the paralysis.

punchline.text: More options can mean fewer decisions.

quiz.question: What is choice overload?
options: Too many options reducing decision quality and satisfaction

details.summary: Having too many options can paralyze decision-making, reduce satisfaction, and increase regret. Sheena Iyengar's famous jam study showed that people were ten times more likely to buy jam when offered 6 options compared to 24. More choice does not always mean more freedom or better outcomes.
details.whyItMatters: Choice overload challenges the assumption that more options are always better. In product design, policy, and daily life, curating fewer high-quality options often leads to better decisions.
takeaways: Too many options can paralyze decision-making
Excess choice reduces satisfaction and increases regret
Iyengar's jam study demonstrated the paradox experimentally

faq.question: Does choice overload always occur with many options?
faq.answer: Not always. When people have clear preferences, expertise, or well-defined criteria, more options can help. Choice overload is strongest when options are similar, the decision is important, there is no clear favorite, and people lack domain expertise.

faq.question: How can choice overload be reduced in product design?
faq.answer: Limit the number of options presented at once. Use categories and filters to organize choices. Provide clear defaults and recommendations. Highlight key differences between options. Progressive disclosure, showing details only when requested, also reduces overwhelm.
